summary: Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Indology. She completed a BA at the University of Vienna, studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and was supervised by Helmut Tauscher for her MA.

E. Adelaide Hahn was a linguist who earned degrees from Hunter College and Columbia University, studying under Edgar Howard Sturtevant, Leonard Bloomfield, and Franklin Edgerton. She served at Hunter College (1915–1963) and was President of the Linguistic Society of America in 1946.

E. Baer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Baer studied at the University of Basel and the University of Zurich (PhD), where teachers included Adolf Kaegi, Jakob Hausheer, Eduard Schwyzer, and Emil Abegg.
E. Easwaran Nampoothiry was an Indologist who studied under S. Venkitasubramonia Iyer. He served as a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Kerala (attested 1973).

E. F. Schumacher was an author and philosopher. He studied at the University of Bonn, New College, London School of Economics, and Columbia University, and was taught by Edward Conze. He held posts at Columbia University (~1933–1934) and the University of Oxford.

E. Gene Smith was a Tibetologist educated at Adelphi, Hobart and William Smith, Utah, and Washington (PhD under Turrell V. Wylie). He served at the Library of Congress (1968–1985, 1994–1997) and founded/directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (1999–2010).
E. H. Hall was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under George Abraham Grierson. Hall worked as a clerk for the India Office Records.
E. H. Rogers was active in linguistics and Indology. Rogers served as Head Master at The Lawrence School, Sanawar (1858) and as a Sub-Inspector for Army Schools (1861).
E. M. Hare was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Stamford School and was a pupil of Frank Lee Woodward.

E. Michael Mendelson was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who taught Jane Bunnag. He was educated at King's College, Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Paris (~1949–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1950–1952).

E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1951–1954) under Johannes Nobel. He held a post at Sri Venkateswara University (attested 1977).

E. Sherman Oakley was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, Airedale Independent College, and the University of Allahabad (M.A.). He joined the London Missionary Society in 1888 and served as Principal of Ramsay College.

E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London (PhD), where he studied under William Stede. In 1934, he became principal of Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Ebbe Oskar Tuneld was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lund University (PhD 1915), Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen (under Hermann Oldenberg), and Paris (under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi). He served as PD and Professor of Indology at Lund.

Ebenezer Burgess studied at Amherst College (~1827–1831) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1834–1837). He served as a missionary with the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions from 1839 to 1854.

Ebenezer Charles Bethlehem Hallam worked in Indology and linguistics after attending King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Toronto Normal School. He served as a missionary with the American Free Baptist Mission (1857–1872) and the Baptist Missionary Society (-1881).

Eberhard Fischer is an Indologist and art historian/archaeologist who earned a PhD at the University of Basel. He served as Director of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and held leadership roles with the Rietberg-Gesellschaft and the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation for Archaeological Research Abroad.

Eberhard Gothein studied at Breslau and Heidelberg under Wilhelm Dilthey. He worked in economics and history, holding professorships in Nationalökonomie at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (1884–1890), the University of Bonn (1890–1905), and Heidelberg University (from 1905).

Eberhard Sandschneider is a sinologist who completed his education and PhD at Saarland University. He held positions at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), the Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader was a linguist who studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen. He held academic posts at Zurich, Giessen, and Jena before serving as Professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).
